description: Basks all day, crusted and cracked open on the light beneath, then gets up breathing fire it never learned.
lore: What fell was small. A damp thing the length of a hand, the colour of wet bark and living under it, no danger to anything and in no danger either. That is the animal, entire. There is nothing whatever in it to account for what is out on the black rock now.

Then it thinned, the way everything here thins, and by the time its own account of itself had gone there was a great deal of everybody else's lying about to take up the slack. A great many of the dead handled a creature like this once, in a great many countries, and nearly all of them handled it the same way: you put a log on the fire, and a little while later something comes running out of the flame. Every one of them drew the obvious conclusion. Not one of them ever went back and checked. So the shape it holds now is theirs, and it stands several times the size the animal was: the hide gone to crust, the crust split along the seams, something in the gaps that is steady rather than flickering, and eyes the same colour as the gaps. When the mouth opens what comes out is fire. It is the same animal all the way through, for all that. Nothing got up out of the warm ground out there to replace it; it fell, once, and it was smaller than a hand.

The hard piece is a coal. Dark rock, cracked through, live red still moving in the seams, and as warm the year after as the day it came out; set into a blade it sets alight whatever the blade touches, and the burning carries on a while after you have stopped. Which is odd on the face of it, the fire on the animal having been somebody else's idea to begin with. Except that it was told into burning and then it burned, every day, for a very long time, and there is no line anywhere in that where the borrowed thing stops and the creature's own habit starts. Everything else it leaves goes cold. The shed teeth, the broad amber fang split from crown to root where it came down on the wrong kind of bone, the foot cut clean off at the joint with its three cream claws: warm in the hand for an hour or two, and then only leavings.

It does not appear to hunt. There is very little on that stretch worth the trouble, and it spends most of a day flat against the warm stone doing nothing at all, which is precisely what the story about it says it should be doing. Then it gets up and walks a round that nothing accounts for, and bites whatever is standing in it. The black rock runs toward the cave and gets warmer the whole way. It walks to the edge of that and turns, every time, and has never gone in.
